blocks.text: Role · Relationship · Time and Place · Tension · Emphasis and Focus
The Elements of Drama are the building blocks of every story. In this strategy, students mix and match them, and in minutes they’ve built a brand-new scene from scratch.

items.text: As a class or in groups, come up with 5–10 ideas for each element.
Pick one idea from each category, or draw them randomly for extra surprise!
See what dramatic scene comes out of the combination.

items: Role: a Teacher and a Scientist
Time and Place: the year 2100, on a spaceship in another galaxy
Tension: the oxygen supply has malfunctioned, and there’s only enough for one of them to make it back to Earth…

Emphasis and Focus: how will you make the audience feel it? Maybe a spotlight shines on the two characters while the rest of the stage goes dark. Maybe music swells to bring out the fear and heartbreak of the moment.

blocks.text: Five simple choices, and suddenly there’s a story the audience can’t look away from!

Students learn the language of drama by using it, not memorizing it. Random combinations spark creativity and laughter. Students also see how changing one element, like the relationship or the tension, can turn a story upside down.
The “in love” relationship works well for our teacher-candidate audience. For younger students, you could swap it for something like “best friends” or “siblings.”
